symptom: a script that builds a domain model spent half its time in Writer.updateUnit: seeding 300 entities and 299 associations took 16 s after the read-side fixes of ako/mxcli#2160, 48% of it rewriting and reconciling a module's whole domain model once per statement
cause: CREATE ENTITY and CREATE ASSOCIATION each rewrite the module's domain model unit, and every rewrite went through canon.Reconcile against the stored unit (identity carry, translation carry, $ID transplant, comparison) and was written. The cost of one statement is the size of the model it adds to, and the profile put it in the reconcile, not in the file write
file: mdl/executor/entity_run.go (new), mdl/executor/executor.go (stepRuns in both statement loops), modelsdk/mpr/writer_deferred.go (DeferUnitWritesJudged, judgeHeld), mdl/backend/modelsdk/backend.go
insight: The held-write run that access rules use (ako/mxcli#872) fits, but its reports are held to the end and these statements report as they go. The first experiment - just add the two statements to the run - cut the stage from 15 s to 6 s with identical first-run output and made every re-run statement say 'Modified' although nothing reached storage (#890 again). So the writer judges each held write as it is held and counts it in WriteStats like a write that landed: the first write of a unit against storage with a real reconcile, later ones against the write the run already holds. Two things made that later comparison wrong before it was right, each found by dumping both documents and diffing them with binaries masked: the two sides must be normalised for storage first (the writer completes what a builder leaves out - a validation rule's empty Message - so a unit rebuilt from storage has it and a freshly declared entity does not), and identity fields must be carried from the previous write. With both, the cheap comparison agrees with the reconcile on a 599-statement re-run. What moves is when a write can fail: the reconcile against storage, and the storage-GUID guard in it, now runs at the end of the run, after the statements have reported. Measured: reconciles 3 -> 2 for two entities and 11 -> 2 for six; the 300-entity seed 17 s -> 10 s on first run and 19 s -> 13 s on a settled re-run, same machine and session.
